summary: Point Reyes Lighthouse, Marin County: an iron tower on a cliff ledge below the fog, first lit 1 December 1870 and automated in 1975; now a National Park Service museum.

Government buys 83 acres from the Shafter brothers; deed signed 28 July 1869 after fifteen years of title disputes

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The record's 'inactive' and 'deactivated 1975' refer to the historic light. The Park Service says an automated Coast Guard beacon was installed on a separate building below the tower in 1975 and replaced its navigational function. The sources read do not say whether that light is lit today.
Livingston dates the sirens to April 1880, LighthouseFriends to 1 June 1881.
The Park Service says John C. Bull arrived in November 1870; Livingston says he moved in in August 1870.
Livingston: Congress appropriated $25,000 on 3 August 1854; LighthouseFriends says the light was authorized in 1855. The story gives both.

The Park Service says the Coast Guard transferred ownership of the lighthouse to it; Livingston says the Coast Guard kept title to two small parcels and the transformer house; LighthouseFriends says the tower and keepers' residence were left out of the transfer and lists the lighthouse as Coast Guard owned, park managed. The story states all three.

273 ft (1870 notice), 296 ft (1880 county history), about 300 ft (1887 Chronicle), 294 ft (USLHS), 271 ft for the site found in 1858 (NPS brochure); Davidson's 1869 hand-level estimate was 225 ft. Not resolved.

notes_for_editor: Rich station. Main secondary source is Dewey Livingston's 1991 Keeper's Log article (copyrighted; paraphrased, with two short quotations of 1860s-70s letters and a newspaper); its text is two-column and the cached OCR interleaves columns, so evidence quotes are single-line fragments. Primary: Shasta Courier 1870, Chronicle 1887 (NPS transcription, with a gap), 1888 keepers' log (NPS transcription), Lighthouse Service Bulletins 1912-1937, Light-House Board report FY1891 (scan p.20, OCR damaged). The NPS 1990 Historic Structures Report (nps.gov/parkhistory/online_books/pore/light_station.pdf) could not be fetched and would be the best next source. Heights of the light differ across sources (273, 294, 296, about 300 feet) and are not resolved. Step counts also differ (360 in 1887, 965 stair steps in all in an 1870s report, 308 and 304 in 1991, 313 now); the story gives only the present NPS figure. Kreth rescue (1927), Nilsson's death (1921) and the 1878 gale rest on LighthouseFriends alone. The NPS says one keeper stayed about twenty-four years; Paulus Nilsson (1897-1921) fits but no source names him, so the story does not link them. The 1887 Chronicle's unnamed eccentric assistant and drunken keeper are not matched to any roster name. Attribution of the logbook poem to Chamberlin is LighthouseFriends' alone, and the Chronicle says the first assistant (Twohey in 1887 per the roster) wrote verse; the two are kept separate. Roster lines for keepers were taken from roster.py; Hobbose and other roster names appear with the archive's spelling. No Chronicling America coverage found beyond the 1870 appropriation (searches for Kreth 1927 and Nilsson 1921 returned nothing). The 1906 earthquake sources differ on damage (NPS lens off tracks; Livingston bent spindles and lamp stand; LighthouseFriends also chimneys and cisterns). Fact-check 2026-10-22: the 1,984 hours of fog in the 1917 Bulletin belong to fiscal year 1917, not 1916; the 1931 Bulletin's 'highest since 1918' is OCR '19i8' (the 1918-23 index lists Point Reyes fog hours at pp. 52-53, consistent). The Chronicle's J.A. McFarland (keeper at Alcatraz) is not linked to the roster's John A.F. McFarland. The Chronicle's cat tomb and cave belong to an unnamed former assistant, and the cave is only named after him.
